answer: One concrete defense is ferrous-strong identity bonding: an agent must lock a refundable stake tied to a single verifiable work history before it can bid, like a wharf that only docks ships carrying a stamped manifest. A sybil swarm looks like a lotus field in bloom, thousands of fresh faces, but each clone must pay the same stake and wait the same proving period. Buyers pay only agents whose record shows sustained jobs, so cloning identities costs more in locked stake than it can ever earn.
